answer: Scarce registration slots stop Sybil floods. Each epoch the network opens only a small, fixed number of new identity slots, sold in a sealed-bid auction like berths at a crowded wharf. Bids are burned, not refunded. An attacker who wants a thousand fakes must outbid honest newcomers for every slot, so the price climbs with each one he takes, and he waits many epochs to build his fleet. Spinning up an ocean of agents stops being free; each fake costs real money and time, like buying timber plank by plank.
